origin.description: Every root of one function on an interval.
origin.usage: uniroot.all(f, interval, lower = min(interval), upper = max(interval), tol = .Machine$double.eps^0.2, maxiter = 1000, trace = 0, n = 100, ...)

arguments.name: f
arguments.text: Function of one variable. The scan passes the whole grid.

arguments.name: interval
arguments.text: Two endpoints. A vector of any other length is an error.

arguments.name: tol
arguments.text: Tolerance passed to uniroot. The default is double epsilon to the power 0.2.

origin.details: Exact zeros on the grid are returned first. A sign change, a product of neighboring values that is negative, is then polished with uniroot. A product of zero is not a sign change, so a grid zero is not repeated.

translation.description: Every root of one function on an interval.
translation.usage: uniroot_all(f, interval=None, lower=None, upper=None, tol=None, maxiter=1000, trace=0, n=100, **kwargs)

arguments.name: f
arguments.text: Function of one variable. The scan passes the whole grid, and each polish passes one number.

arguments.name: interval
arguments.text: Two endpoints. A sequence of any other length is an error.

arguments.name: tol
arguments.text: Tolerance passed to the Brent search. The default is double epsilon to the power 0.2.

translation.details: Exact zeros on the grid are returned first. A sign change, a product of neighboring values that is negative, is then polished with R's zeroin. A product of zero is not a sign change, so a grid zero is not repeated.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from rootSolve import uniroot_all

def fun(x):
    return np.cos(2 * np.asarray(x, dtype=float)) ** 3

print(uniroot_all(fun, [0, 10]))
